{
  "research_question": "How do the five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: Perform one-way ANOVA to test for mean differences across the 5 stimulation paradigms.",
    "For Success: Perform one-way ANOVA to test for mean differences in Success rates across the 5 stimulation paradigms.",
    "For Path Efficiency: Perform one-way ANOVA to test for mean differences across the 5 stimulation paradigms.",
    "For Average Speed: Perform one-way ANOVA to test for mean differences across the 5 stimulation paradigms.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): Perform one-way ANOVA to test for mean differences across the 5 stimulation paradigms."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check Normality: Verify that residuals for each response variable approximate a normal distribution using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests. Note that Time-to-Target ranges from 0.5 to 201.4 and Path Efficiency from 0.001 to 29.8, suggesting potential skewness; if severe, consider non-parametric alternatives like Kruskal-Wallis.",
    "Check Homogeneity of Variances: Perform Levene's test or Brown-Forsythe test for each response variable to ensure variances are equal across the 5 groups. High variance in 'Success' (binary logit issues) or 'Path Efficiency' (bounded 0-30) may violate this.",
    "Check Independence: Verify that observations (rows) are independent based on the experimental design (N=76,655 rows)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus ANOVA F-test is significant (p < 0.05) for any response variable, proceed with pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test for multiple comparisons to control the family-wise error rate across the 5 paradigms.",
    "Flag specific differences expected: Based on summary stats, Strong effect is expected for Sham compared to others in Time-to-Target (Mean ~4.68 vs ~2.5-3.1) and Success (Mean ~0.27 vs ~0.68-0.78).",
    "Interpret AD: Compare mean Angular Dispersion (Sham: 0.236 vs Combined: 0.399) to determine if stimulation reduces spatial randomness."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham paradigm is expected to have significantly higher Time-to-Target (4.68s) compared to Combined (2.56s), ICMS Only (3.05s), and Dim Visual Only (3.14s).",
    "Sham paradigm is expected to have significantly lower Success rate (0.273) compared to all other paradigms (0.67-0.78).",
    "Average Speed is expected to be lower in Sham (10.74) compared to Combined (12.83) and ICMS Only (12.04).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in Sham (0.236) and highest in Combined (0.399), suggesting navigation paths in Sham are less dispersed angularly, despite lower success.",
    "Bright Visual Only (n=3323) and Sham (n=3505) have much smaller sample sizes than Combined (n=48846), increasing uncertainty in estimates for these groups."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Skewed Distributions: Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency have wide ranges; ANOVA assumes normality which may be violated.",
    "Binary Data: Success is a bounded binary variable (0-1); ANOVA on raw proportions is less powerful than regression-based approaches or transforming data.",
    "Unequal Sample Sizes: The 'Bright Visual Only' and 'Sham' groups have substantially fewer trials (3,323 and 3,505) compared to 'Combined' (48,846), potentially reducing statistical power and violating robust ANOVA assumptions if imbalance is extreme.",
    "Bounded Variables: Path Efficiency (max 29.81, min 0.001) and AD (max 1.0, min 0.0006) are bounded, which can distort variance estimates if the bulk of data lies near boundaries."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a General Linear Model (GLM) or Mixed-Effects Model where Mouse ID is treated as a random effect to account for repeated measures within mice, and response variables are modeled with appropriate distributions (e.g., Binomial link for Success, Gamma or Inverse Gaussian for positive skewed continuous variables like Time-to-Target)."
}
